title: The Goose That Laid the Golden Eggs
summary: A poor man finds a special bird that gives him golden eggs every single day.
coverScene: A poor farmer looks with wide eyes at a golden egg resting in a simple straw nest beside a goose.

sentences.text: Once upon a time, a poor farmer lived in a small house near a quiet village.
His life was very hard.
He had little money to buy food.
However, everything changed when a special bird arrived at his farm.
Every single morning, the man walked to the place.
To his great surprise, he found a fine egg waiting there.
He took the important object to the town market.
He sold it for money.
As days passed, the farmer slowly grew rich because the bird laid one egg each day.
He was able to buy good food, new clothes, and a better home.
Yet, despite having so much money, the man became very angry and fast.
He wanted to have all the money at once instead of waiting.
Thinking that the bird must be full of money, a strange idea came into his mind.
If he cut the animal open, he would find a huge amount of money.
Without thinking, the man took a sharp tool and cut the animal open.
To his bad surprise, he found that it was just an ordinary bird.
Now the bird was gone, and there were no more eggs left.
The sad farmer sat down in deep pain and cried over his mistake.
His own bad mind had cost him everything.
He was left as poor as before.
From that day forward, he learned that people must not act so fast.
He lost everything because he wanted more and more every single day.
If he had been happy, he would have lived a long and good life.
Instead, he destroyed his own future with his hands.
Now he has nothing left in his empty home.
He sits alone every night and thinks about his big mistake.
He remembers the wonderful eggs that he sold at the market.
He wishes that he had not cut the special bird open.
If he had waited, he would have received more money.
Now his life is hard again, and he has no money for food.
He looks around the empty room and feels deep pain.
The poor man understands that wanting too much brings only trouble and pain.
He promises to be patient if he ever receives another chance.
However, time does not turn back for anyone.
He must live with the result of his poor action.
The sun sets behind the hills, and dark night covers the small house.
He closes his eyes and tries to sleep through the cold hours.
Every morning brings a new day, but no shiny egg waits for him now.
He works in the fields from morning until evening to earn a little food.
His friends feel sorry for him, but they cannot fix his problem.
He has learned a hard lesson about the danger of wanting too much.
Life continues to move forward, and the farmer remains poor until the end of his days.
He has worked hard for many years, but the past cannot change.
He has lost his best friend, and he has found only regret.
If he had taken care of the animal, he would have lived a rich life.
Instead, his own action has brought him back to the beginning.
He looks at the empty place where the animal used to stay.
He hopes that someone might help him, but no one comes.
The quiet village stays the same while the poor man sits and thinks about his lost future.

sentences.text: Once upon a time, a poor farmer lived in a small house near a quiet village.
His life was very hard, and he had little money to buy food for himself.
However, everything changed when a special bird arrived at his farm.
Every single morning, the farmer walked to the place where the animal stayed.
To his great surprise, he found a bright golden egg waiting there for him.
He took the valuable object to the town market and sold it for a lot of money.
As days passed, the farmer slowly grew rich because the bird laid one golden egg each day.
He was able to buy good food, new clothes, and a better home for his life.
Yet, despite having so much wealth, the man became very rushed and hurried.
He wanted to have all the gold at once instead of waiting for one egg per day.
Thinking that the bird must be full of gold inside, a strange and silly idea came into his mind.
If he cut the animal open, he believed that he would find a huge collection of gold.
Without thinking about the consequences, the man took a sharp knife and cut the creature open.
To his absolute shock, he found that it was just an ordinary bird with nothing special inside.
Now the animal was gone, and there were no more golden eggs left for him.
The silly farmer sat down in deep sadness and cried over his terrible mistake.
His own desire had cost him everything, leaving him as poor as he was before.
From that day forward, he learned that being hurried and wanting too much destroy wonderful gifts.
The farmer had lived in that small house for many years.
His daily routine was simple before the bird arrived.
He worked hard every day just to get enough food.
When the first golden egg appeared, his entire world changed.
He could not believe his eyes when he saw the bright object.
Every morning brought a new chance to improve his poor life.
The local market was full of people who wanted to buy things from him.
He received a large amount of money for each sale.
Soon, he bought nice clothes and good food for his daily meals.
His neighbors watched him become rich in a short period of time.
They wondered how a poor man could suddenly afford such a nice house.
The farmer kept the secret of the bird to himself.
He did not want anyone else to know about the golden eggs.
However, money often changes how a person thinks and acts.
The farmer grew more and more rushed with every passing week.
He felt that one egg per day was simply not enough for his growing needs.
His mind was filled with thoughts of incredible wealth.
He imagined that the inside of the bird must contain a mountain of gold.
If he waited any longer, he feared that he might lose his chance to be very rich.
That silly thought made him take the sharp knife from his kitchen table.
He did not listen to any voice of reason in his head.
His hands were shaking as he approached the animal in the small space.
He made the terrible cut without a single second of delay.
Blood and hair were everywhere, but there was no gold to be seen.
Only an ordinary creature lay dead on the floor of the room.
The terrible truth hit him like a heavy blow from above.
He realized that his own actions had destroyed his only source of wealth.
No more eggs would ever be found in that place.
His brilliant future was gone in less than a minute.
He sat on the ground and cried for a very long time.
The sadness stayed with him until the end of his days.
People in the village talked about his big mistake for generations.
Everyone agreed that being too rushed always leads to complete ruin.
The farmer remained poor for the rest of his life.
He never forgot the terrible lesson that he had learned.
Stories like this are told to children all across the country.
They teach important lessons about life and human behavior.
When people want too much, they often lose what they already have.
Time is a quality that helps individuals make better decisions.
If the farmer had been quiet, he would have lived a comfortable life.
Instead, his mind was clouded by a strong desire for rapid wealth.
We should always appreciate the good things that come to us naturally.
Trying to force success usually results in total failure.
The poor farmer learned this truth the hardest way possible.
His story remains a clear warning for anyone who feels too rushed.
May we all remember to value what we have today.
Tomorrow is never promised, so we must be careful with our choices.

sentences.text: For many long years, a humble farmer inhabited a modest dwelling on the quiet outskirts of a forgotten village.
His existence was defined by relentless labor, as he toiled from dawn until dusk merely to secure his daily bread.
Poverty was a heavy cloak that he wore through every changing season, leaving him little hope for a better future.
Yet fate is often capricious, and the entire trajectory of his life shifted the moment an extraordinary avian creature arrived at his farm.
He had never witnessed such brilliant plumage, nor had he ever imagined that a simple animal could alter his lonely world so completely.
Every single morning without fail, the farmer walked toward the shadowed corner of the yard where the creature rested.
To his absolute astonishment, a gleaming orb of pure gold lay nestled upon the straw, radiating a warm and impossible light.
He would pick up the heavy, precious object with trembling fingers, marveling at the sheer fortune that had literally been deposited at his feet.
Before this miraculous arrival, his daily routine had been remarkably simple and utterly devoid of any financial relief.
Now, however, he possessed a treasure that defied explanation and promised to lift him far above his previous struggles.
Carrying the radiant prize concealed beneath a worn woolen coat, he made his way to the bustling town market whenever the sun climbed high.
The local merchants were immediately captivated by the exceptional purity of the metal he offered for exchange.
He received a remarkably large sum of money for each individual sale, transforming his financial standing almost overnight.
Within a remarkably short period, he was able to acquire fine garments that replaced his threadbare rags and purchase provisions that far exceeded his basic needs.
His neighbors watched his sudden ascent with growing fascination, wondering how a man who had been destitute for decades could suddenly afford such comfortable living conditions.
Wisely choosing to keep the origin of his newfound wealth entirely to himself, the farmer offered vague explanations for his sudden prosperity.
He feared that any intrusion from the outside world might jeopardize the singular source of his fortune.
As weeks melted into months, the steady accumulation of gold began to work a subtle and corrosive change within his mind.
Money has a peculiar way of altering human perception, and the farmer soon found himself consumed by an obsessive urgency.
The steady rhythm of receiving one magnificent egg each morning no longer satisfied the growing hunger that echoed in his chest.
He grew increasingly impatient with the passage of time, feeling that the natural pace of his enrichment was far too slow.
His thoughts became entirely dominated by the vast fortune that he imagined must be resting just beneath the surface of the bird's quiet exterior.
It seemed entirely illogical to him that such a miraculous creature should only yield a single treasure per day when a vast reservoir of wealth must surely be hidden inside.
If he waited any longer, he convinced himself, some unforeseen misfortune might rob him of the opportunity to claim his entire inheritance at once.
His mind was completely clouded by a frantic desire for immediate and absolute abundance.
One fateful morning, as the pale sunlight filtered through the cracked window of his small kitchen, the temptation reached an intolerable peak.
Without pausing to entertain a single sensible doubt, his trembling hand reached for the sharpest steel blade resting upon the wooden table.
He ignored the quiet voice of reason that whispered from the depths of his conscience, choosing instead to listen only to the demands of his relentless greed.
His footsteps were heavy and hurried as he crossed the small space that separated him from the unsuspecting creature.
Not a single second of hesitation delayed the devastating movement of his hand.
The sharp metal cut swiftly through the air, bringing an abrupt and tragic end to the quiet life that had sustained his own.
As the terrible deed was done, the farmer stared in mounting horror at the harsh reality revealed before his wide eyes.
There was no towering mountain of gold hidden within, nor any secret chamber filled with glittering treasures.
Instead, he found only an ordinary bird, identical to any other creature that roamed the fields beyond his fence.
The heavy realization of his own destructive folly struck him with the force of a falling stone.
A profound and suffocating silence descended upon the small room as the full magnitude of his error became unmistakably clear.
His brilliant future, built upon patience and daily grace, had vanished entirely in less than a single minute of reckless haste.
No more golden eggs would ever grace his property, and the generous gift he had so foolishly abused was gone forever.
He sank slowly to the dusty wooden floor, burying his face in his hands as bitter tears of regret began to fall.
The sadness that washed over him was deep and permanent, promising to accompany him through every remaining day of his life.
Word of the tragic event spread quickly through the village, becoming a cautionary tale told and retold across generations.
The neighbors who had once envied his sudden wealth now shook their heads in sorrow at the extent of his self-inflicted ruin.
Everyone in the community agreed that an uncontrolled desire for rapid gain invariably leads to total destruction.
The farmer remained as poor for the rest of his days as he had been before the strange bird ever crossed his threshold.
He never forgot the harsh lesson he had taught himself through an act of supreme impatience.
Tales of this nature are frequently shared with younger listeners across the country to impart vital truths about human behavior.
When individuals allow themselves to be consumed by the desire for more than they truly need, they frequently forfeit the blessings they already possess.
Time is a gentle quality that allows thoughtful people to make balanced and beneficial decisions.
Had the farmer chosen to remain content with his daily fortune, he would have lived a remarkably comfortable and peaceful life.
Instead, his vision was entirely obscured by the blinding mist of sudden greed.
We should always cultivate a deep appreciation for the natural gifts that come to us without the need for force.
Attempting to rush success or demand immediate rewards usually results in complete and irreversible failure.
The impoverished farmer absorbed this painful reality in the most direct and unforgiving manner possible.
His unfortunate experience serves as a clear warning for anyone who feels pressured by the frantic pace of modern ambition.
May we all remember to cherish what we hold today, knowing that tomorrow depends entirely upon the wisdom of our choices.
